title: Cap-blocked draft INSERT silently drops the save; handler still answers ok:true
evidence:
+INSERT INTO application_draft (vacancy_id, email, fields, continue_token)
+SELECT $1::uuid, lower($2), $3::jsonb, $4
+WHERE EXISTS (
+    SELECT 1 FROM application_draft d
+    WHERE d.vacancy_id = $1::uuid AND d.email = lower($2)
+  )
+  OR (
+    SELECT count(*) FROM application_draft d
+    WHERE d.vacancy_id = $1::uuid
+  ) < 500
 ... handler:
+                  case
+                    sql.upsert_application_draft(
+                      config.db,
+                      vacancy_uuid,
+                      applicant_email,
+                      fields_to_json(filtered),
+                      wisp.random_string(48),
+                    )
+                  {
+                    Ok(_) -> {
detail: At the 500/vacancy cap the INSERT...SELECT yields zero rows; upsert returns Ok(Returned(_, [])) and handle_save_draft maps any Ok(_) to {"ok":true}. The endpoint is unauthenticated so the cap is attacker-fillable; legit saves then vanish while the client reports success.
recommended_fix: Match on empty RETURNING from the upsert and answer ok:false (or 503) for cap-blocked inserts; keep the silent-200 only for the submitted/erased guard case.

title: Fan-out subquery counts stamped draft rows, not sends — documented "max 3 continue emails per recipient per hour" is not enforced
evidence:
+-- (max 3 continue emails per recipient per hour across ALL vacancies: the
 ...
+  AND (
+    last_link_sent_at IS NULL
+    OR last_link_sent_at < now() - interval '10 minutes'
+  )
+  AND (
+    SELECT count(*) FROM application_draft d2
+    WHERE d2.email = lower($2)
+      AND d2.last_link_sent_at IS NOT NULL
+      AND d2.last_link_sent_at > now() - interval '1 hour'
+  ) < 3
detail: The <3 check counts rows stamped in the last hour. One draft re-sends every 10 minutes (6/hr) while its count stays 1; two drafts sustain 12/hr. Only a third distinct draft trips the bound, so the advertised per-recipient ceiling is overshot up to 4x.
recommended_fix: Count actual sends (append a send-event row per claim, or a sends counter per recipient) or rewrite the comment to state the real invariant: per-draft 10-minute cooldown plus max 3 distinct drafts stamped per hour.

title: 500/vacancy draft cap counts stripped (submitted) and tombstoned rows that persist until vacancy close
evidence:
+  OR (
+    SELECT count(*) FROM application_draft d
+    WHERE d.vacancy_id = $1::uuid
+  ) < 500
 ... strip_draft_on_submit.sql:
+-- empty the draft's PII payload, kill the continue token, and stamp the
+-- resume→submit metric. The row itself stays (email + timestamps only)
+-- until the retention sweep removes it at vacancy close.
 ... erase_draft_by_token.sql:
+-- (vacancy, email) key is kept as a suppression record until the retention
+-- sweep removes it at vacancy close
detail: The cap subquery has no submitted_at/erased_at filter, while submit-strip and erasure both retain the row until vacancy close. Every submission or erasure permanently burns a cap slot; ~500 lifetime applicants disables new drafts for the vacancy's entire life.
recommended_fix: Add AND d.submitted_at IS NULL AND d.erased_at IS NULL to the cap count subquery so only live drafts consume the budget.

title: resumed_at stamped for empty-fields continue-link payload but not for the identical save payload
detail: handle_save_draft's empty-filtered branch returns before the resume_token stamp; handle_continue_link stamps it for the same payload despite the "Same re-engagement stamp" comment. The drafts-resumed funnel diverges by endpoint for identical client state.
recommended_fix: Hoist the resumed_at stamp ahead of the filtered-fields branch in both handlers, or skip it in both when the payload carried no usable fields.

title: Dead COALESCEs: claim RETURNING and list_resumable SELECT cannot observe a NULL continue_token
evidence:
claim:
+SET continue_token = COALESCE(continue_token, $3),
 ...
+RETURNING COALESCE(continue_token, '') AS continue_token;
 list_resumable:
+SELECT email, COALESCE(continue_token, '') AS continue_token
+FROM application_draft
+WHERE vacancy_id = $1::uuid
+  AND submitted_at IS NULL
+  AND continue_token IS NOT NULL;
 handler guard:
+      Ok(token) if token != "" -> application_url <> "/resume/" <> token
detail: The SET clause already guarantees non-NULL on returned rows, and the IS NOT NULL filter makes the SELECT COALESCE dead; the inbound handler's token != "" guard then defends an impossible empty string. Noise that obscures the mint-at-save invariant.
recommended_fix: Return/select continue_token bare and drop the empty-string guard, or keep one defensive COALESCE with a comment naming the legacy NULL case it protects.

title: File-slot filter defines 5 primary document slots but only 2 co-applicant prefixes
evidence:
+pub fn file_slot_names() -> List(String) {
+  [
+    "proof_of_income_primary",
+    "landlord_ref_primary",
+    "character_ref_primary",
+    "employer_ref_primary",
+    "additional_docs",
+  ]
+}
+
+const coapplicant_slot_prefixes = [
+  "proof_of_income_coapplicant_", "employer_ref_coapplicant_",
+]
 ... stated purpose:
+/// skips type=file controls; the server filter drops these names too, so a
+/// hand-crafted JSON payload can't park anything under a document slot's
+/// identity
detail: The filter's own slot taxonomy spans income/landlord/character/employer/additional, yet co-applicant coverage is limited to income and employer prefixes. The comment's universal claim ("can't park anything under a document slot's identity") outruns what the filter blocks.
recommended_fix: Add landlord_ref_coapplicant_ and character_ref_coapplicant_ (and the co-applicant additional-docs naming if one exists) to coapplicant_slot_prefixes, or narrow the comment.
